title: Audit: in-repo HPE checkers do not read the pre-wrapper recipe
head: 94d77d2cf19b5fbf3d14cd145fc5fd6ad8d24bd6
body:
## Summary
- States the boundary lemma already proved as `factor_iff_pre`: after (N), the wrapped block equals `C₇ ⊗ id` if and only if the executed pre-wrapper recipe `R'` equals the certified recipe `R`.
- Shows that `scripts/verify_hpe_lean_binding.py` and `research/hyperplane-end-lean/code/check_hpe_pairs.py` never read that recipe. A synthetic 38-helper word whose records name `E:FULL` is accepted by both, and deleting the record is also accepted.
- A changed adapter phase and an `h += p` gate are rejected, so the checkers do see monomials and the tail coefficient. They do not discharge `hrec` in `hpe_word_exact`.

No new kappa and no selected-frontier change. Seed `d9b349359a3c923c0212b9514fe130b3`, scope key `e3ffea67887eeb4c396c`, base `b5ea56e0a5ac4552166253b1fa4be0753bb38c30`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2703

Overlap refresh on 2026-10-15 covered 782 open PRs and 1329 discussions. Neighboring work is the finished semantic port of the three Clifford pairs (#1394, PR #1415) and the HPE axiom-probe audit (#1593). Neither is this checker-versus-`hrec` gap.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -B research/hpe-prewrapper-binding/verify.py` prints `PASS_HPE_PREWRAPPER_BINDING full_recipe_accepted=true record_optional=true phase_rejected=true coefficient_rejected=true pairs=3`
- [x] `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/hpe-prewrapper-binding --check-only`
- [x] Python 3.12 registered replay: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/hpe-prewrapper-binding outcome=negative-result`
- [ ] Selected baseline was not rerun: this sparse checkout lacks `research/community-frontier1094-audit/ASSEMBLY.json`. Selected record sha256 remains `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

## Limits
The witness is synthetic, not an emitted word. The external control `hpe_pre_wrapper_resolved_to_full_recipe` is not rerun and is not claimed to be absent from the HPE tools. Footprints, well-labelled prefixes and the unit row stay assumptions. Predecessor credit stays with Jeremy Kothe.
